research_question: Using only the complete current scan, can scene-supported observation-conditioned relationships on original returns improve real anomaly-versus-normal ranking over the same backbone and ordinary relationships, and do retained-normal pairing and live-batch tail ranking add transferable benefits?

micro_learning.question: Can the full conditional model learn the task with detection and mean retained-normal supervision, and is there early transfer?
micro_learning.group_scope: all group counts use the step-256 full-206 threshold -4.007288455963135; 201 full FPR at that threshold is 1.2158266699735862 percent, not its own 1-percent operating point; witness lists are partial, overlapping, existing measured slots, not all complex normals

query_exposure.scope: query occurrences including repeats, not unique returns or gradient influence

micro_learning.real_sequence_scope: eight fixed development frames per sequence; each sequence curve uses its own complete point pool; not an independent test set
micro_learning.conclusion: Full-training-pool ranking learning is demonstrated and includes few-return and sparse-normal-paired anomalies. Relative-to-initial ranking transfer exists on fixed 201 and real development scopes, with all 19 sequence curves improving AP and FPR95. Transfer detection loss increases and complex-normal false positives remain high. This is one random seed and a micro subset, not evidence isolating mean pairing or sensor conditioning, nor release of full training.
micro_learning.decision: There is a basis to discuss a potential 1024-update short-learning stage, requiring a separate user decision and a fresh copy of the saved random initial state. It is not authorized or executed. Stop after this micro report.
